references.text: The Israelites forgot the Lord their God and served the Baals and the Asherah poles, using the same phrasing about doing what was evil in the Lord's sight.
Repeats the phrase that the people of Israel did what was evil in the Lord's sight, a recurring theme in the book of Judges.
Once again, the people of Israel do what is evil in the Lord's sight, part of the cyclical structure in the book of Judges.
The same phrasing is used again regarding Israel's apostasy and sin against the Lord.
The Israelites served the Baals and abandoned the Lord, a direct parallel to the Baal worship mentioned in the verse.
Israel attached themselves to Baal-Peor, an early example of Baal worship among the people of Israel.
Solomon followed foreign gods and the Baals, the consequence of doing what was evil in the Lord's sight.
King Ahab served Baal and bowed down to him, fulfilling the pattern of Baal worship.
Israel abandoned the Lord and served Baal, the same sin described in Judges.
The prophet Jeremiah refers to their following the Baals, a prophetic judgment against that same idolatry.
Hosea speaks of Israel's Baal worship and how they forgot the Lord, the same theme as in Judges.
